item.title: Trump’s Big Bend Border Project Paused After Bulldozers Arrive
item.description: The Trump administration is pausing work on a border security project inside Texas’ Big Bend National Park, days after bulldozers began clearing land in one of the least-crossed stretches of the US-Mexico border.

item.title: US High-Grade Bond Sales Set August Record in Year Full of Them
item.description: US investment-grade bond sales have set a third straight monthly record, continuing the market’s fastest pace of issuance as spending on the artificial-intelligence buildout fuels corporate borrowing.

item.title: Traders Alert for Deeper Bond Rout Fueling Niche Arbitrage Trade
item.description: An extended selloff in the $31 trillion US government bond market is opening the door for a potentially lucrative trade that profits from pricing shifts between derivatives and their underlying cash bonds.

item.title: The Two Megatrends Changing the US Treasury Market
item.description: Heading for higher yields.

item.title: Puerto Rico Democrat Seeks Answers on Water Loss, Federal Funds
item.description: Puerto Rico’s representative on Capitol Hill wants to know why the island’s state-run sewer authority loses approximately 60% of the water it produces before it reaches homes, despite federal investment from Washington as far back as 2021 to upgrade its ailing infrastructure system.

item.title: Guggenheim Ties Sink Bonds of $135 Billion Life Insurer Sammons
item.description: Bonds of Sammons Financial Group fell to the lowest since they were issued in June after a report probed the life insurer’s connections to Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners.

item.title: Sonos Plans New Soundbar Ahead of September Hardware Reveal
item.description: Sonos Inc. said in a regulatory document that it is working on a new soundbar, offering the first details about a product that’s likely to make its formal debut during the audio company’s hardware launch in September.

item.title: Andreessen Horowitz Focus of DOJ Probe Over Board Directors
item.description: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is the focus of a Justice Department antitrust probe over whether its investment partners are improperly serving on the boards of competing artificial intelligence companies, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US Bond Selloff Drives 30-Year Yields to the Highest Since 2007
item.description: The yield on 30-year US Treasuries hit the highest in almost two decades, reflecting investor angst over the surging national debt, a flood of long-dated bond sales and inflation that’s been stuck over the Federal Reserve’s target for the past five years.

item.title: Vitol Makes Push Into Data-Center Infrastructure With US Deal
item.description: Vitol said its renewables arm had acquired a data center campus in South Carolina from Meridan Gridworks, one of the first instances of a major commodity trader delving into artificial intelligence infrastructure.

item.title: Microsoft-Tied ‘Project Odyssey’ Bond Lures Buyers at Junk Yield
item.description: A corporate-bond sale dubbed “Project Odyssey” may be increased to $3.9 billion as junk-like yields on the Microsoft Corp.-linked data-center financing drew more than twice that amount in demand.

item.title: Hydro-Quebec Reaches $36 Billion Energy Deal With Newfoundland
item.description: The Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador managed to boost the value of a new 50-year electricity supply agreement with Hydro-Quebec, likely ending a long-running dispute with the province of Quebec.

item.title: Citadel Securities Says Spiking Yields Reflect Fed Policy Risk
item.description: The Federal Reserve’s reluctance to tighten monetary policy after a prolonged period of above-target inflation is keeping long-term bond yields at multiyear highs, posing a broader risk to markets, according to Citadel Securities.

item.title: Goldman Margin Loan Eased Nashville College’s Liquidity Crunch
item.description: Belmont University tapped Goldman Sachs Group Inc. for a margin loan this summer to raise cash, in a sign that even larger universities are facing budget strains.

item.title: SoftBank Invests $200 Million in Construction Startup Gravis Robotics
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. has invested $200 million in Gravis Robotics, a Swiss startup that makes autonomous software for construction machinery.

item.title: Casas Bahia Files for Bankruptcy on High Rates, Tight Credit
item.description: Grupo Casas Bahia SA filed for bankruptcy protection in Sao Paulo, after an out-of-court debt restructuring with its main creditors proved insufficient to resolve its financial troubles.

item.title: Ares Takes Control of UK Taxpayer-Backed Fiber Company Toob
item.description: Ares Management Corp. is taking control of Toob Ltd., the struggling broadband company backed by the UK’s National Wealth Fund, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Shein Is Said to Target Up to $27 Billion Valuation in HK IPO
item.description: Fast-fashion retailer Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is targeting a valuation in the range of $26 billion to $27 billion in its initial public offering in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter, a sharp drop from its peak value.

item.title: Nvidia to Invest Up to $105 Billion for OpenAI Data Center in Ohio
item.description: Nvidia Corp. has agreed to spend as much as $105 billion to support a massive new data center campus in Ohio set to be leased by OpenAI, according to a financial filing, marking the latest tie-up between two dominant forces driving the AI boom.

item.title: Glencore Backed Radiant World With Warrants Deal in Late 2025
item.description: Glencore Plc last year acquired warrants that would have given it a minority ownership stake in Radiant World, the iron ore trader under pressure amid concerns it provided falsified documents to banks, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Blackstone, Blue Owl Private Credit Funds Offer High-Grade Bonds
item.description: Two private credit funds are offering investment-grade bonds Monday, following a lull of such deals to start the third quarter.

item.title: US Homebuilder Sentiment Barely Rises as Costs Stymie Sector
item.description: Homebuilder sentiment in the US barely improved this month as elevated construction and borrowing costs continued to restrain the housing market.

item.title: Saudis Offer Oil From Near Oman in Possible Sign of Shuttling
item.description: Saudi Arabia is offering to sell oil from off the coast of Oman, a sign that the kingdom may be following the United Arab Emirates in shuttling more barrels through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Saylor’s Strategy Sells More Stock to Repurchase Preferred
item.description: Michael Saylor continues to run his Bitcoin accumulation flywheel in reverse.

item.title: Verizon Rebuffed by Supreme Court on $47 Million FCC Refund
item.description: The US Supreme Court refused to let Verizon Communications Inc. try to recoup $47 million it paid after being accused of privacy violations by the Federal Communications Commission.

item.title: Deutsche Telekom to Buy Macquarie’s Poland Fiber, TV Assets in €1 Billion Deal
item.description: Deutsche Telekom AG agreed to buy a fiber company and a television provider in Poland from Macquarie Asset Management for an enterprise value around €1 billion ($1.2 billion), part of the German company’s strategy to expand its broadband offering.

item.title: HKEX Renews CEO Chan’s Contract for Three Years Amid IPO Boom
item.description: Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing Ltd. has renewed Chief Executive Officer Bonnie Chan’s contract from March 2027 through February 2030, according to a statement Monday.

item.title: US Futures Flat; Tech Shares Gain on Anthropic Revenue Jump
item.description: US stock futures were mostly little changed before the bell on Monday, with technology stocks breaking out to the upside as details of Anthropic’s surging sales growth stoked bullish sentiment around AI.

item.title: Canada Inflation Ticks Up to 3% Amid Higher Gas Prices
item.description: Canada’s inflation rate edged up to 3% as the Middle East conflict continued to push up gasoline prices, while core measures of price growth remained subdued.

item.title: Groq Valued at $3.5 Billion in Funding Round After Nvidia Deal
item.description: Groq has raised $350 million in funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, roughly half what it was worth nearly a year ago before Nvidia Corp. struck a licensing deal with the startup and hired away much of its talent.The financing, set to be announced Monday, was led by Dallas-based investment firm Disruptive.
